event.summary: Old tmux terminals lose restart history (specified behavior)
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Restart of a session whose old tmux terminal was ended starts without its old terminal history. Details: assigned patch removes TmuxSeedFault and the tmux_seed_gate/tmux_seed_fault hooks and narrows RelaunchPlan.seed to host history (core.rs:4003–4017); this retires the path that copied history from an old tmux pane. Suggested bucket: highest if loss of retained terminal output is treated as loss of user-owned work; could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed from source and explicit specification, not execution. proposed_drop: SPEC.md, Lifecycle operations, lines 1951–1953 explicitly says: "When the terminal no longer exists (the process that kept it ended, after a reboot, or an old terminal this release ended, see [Terminal experience](#terminal-experience)), Restart starts with an empty one." SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, says "This release ends them at startup (below); every terminal runs in a terminal host" and "The running supervisor runs no tmux at all, and its driver of the old terminals is gone". This candidate concerns the intentional removal of history migration only; it does not claim an independent defect in old terminals or startup killing. possible_cover: none searched. Caveat: requires independent drop check because the consequence could be highest.

event.summary: Removing fresh-claim flag preserves ownership fencing
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether dropping the fresh-versus-reused claim flag permits startup to mutate another process's state or terminate healthy terminals. Source analysis: core.rs:1343–1374 still canonicalizes, reuses an in-process Arc, and takes the same exclusive OS lock for a new claim; another process still yields None. core.rs:6084–6184 still gates store migration and old-terminal ending/reconciliation on ownership.is_some(). The removed flag was documented in the parent as solely gating stale tmux control-client reaping; this runtime no longer starts tmux clients. No new cross-process ownership route is introduced by the assigned signature simplification. Suggested bucket: highest if a route existed (termination of user processes or database migration under an incumbent). could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for this narrow concern; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation above, not a specification exception. possible_cover: none. Caveat: same-process constructors deliberately share ownership; production has one Supervisor per process (core.rs:1276–1291), unchanged by the patch.

event.summary: Host-only launch excerpts do not need the tmux history fence
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing the per-launch excerpt fence can attach an earlier run's output to a new launch failure. Source: the assigned patch removes RunCells.launch_excerpt and its fresh initialization from relaunched_entry. The replacement append_launch_excerpt (service/launch_artifacts.rs:42–76) reads only the held host's visible screen after HostEvidence::Owned { dead: true }, not retained history; status.rs:637–652 invokes it only for the inferred never-started shape. Host terminals run one child and Restart seeds only scrollback above a blank screen, as specified in SPEC_impl.md, Launch failure classification: "A host runs one child for its whole life, so everything on its screen is this launch's output" and "a Restart's new host starts with a blank screen, so no quote reaches back into the previous run." Thus the old tmux pane-reuse provenance concern has no new-launch route in this type narrowing. Suggested bucket: other (misleading failure detail if a route existed); could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed source/contract analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation and explicit quoted host contract. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not audit the entire restart rollback implementation; host-restart implementation belongs to adjacent groups.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Need check actual guarded call sites and terminology to decide whether this is a concrete false locking contract or whether 'terminal call' has a narrower defined meaning excluding these operations. event.summary: Host-scan lock map forbids the terminal calls its fence must span
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: The rewritten lock-order map tells maintainers not to make terminal calls while holding the host-scan fence, although that fence must stay held while terminal hosts start and are adopted. This is an incorrect internal locking contract, not an observed runtime locking failure. Details: assigned patch lines 982–988 (original core.rs:4581–4583) changes the old prohibition on acquiring 'a tmux call' under host_scan to 'a terminal call'. The new blanket prohibition contradicts the intentional host-only synchronization. core/host_launch.rs:536 takes the shared spawning guard, :537–579 starts and finishes the host, and :609 calls HostTerminal::adopt with that same guard still live. core/host_handover.rs:722–728 takes the exclusive guard expressly through adoption, :732 scans host connections and :786–790 invokes HostTerminal::adopt_found under it. core.rs:4794–4817 explains why this is required: scans take over a host's connection and must not race a spawn before its publication. SPEC_impl.md:2302–2306 likewise requires host_scan to span host starts until publication and directory scans/removals to hold it exclusively. The predecessor wording prohibited tmux calls, which are outside the host lifecycle; replacing that with all terminal calls newly makes the documented rule contradict the required operations. A maintainer following the prohibition could release the fence too early; no such current implementation defect or work-loss consequence is asserted. Suggested fix: remove or scope the obsolete external-call restriction, retaining the actual lock acquisition order and explicitly allowing the host operations the fence protects. Suggested bucket: other/documentation correctness. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from the text; the established issue is a false safety/locking explanation. Confidence: confirmed source and contract analysis; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: no matching record in the supplied complete interface snapshot; no prohibited coverage sources searched. Caveats: correct current runtime code does not refute this documentation defect. No separate broad lock-order audit is claimed. This revision closes the readily source-checkable lead; later-revision persistence remains to be checked, but the reviewed intermediate discrepancy is established.
